---
title: "Secrets"
description: "Add API keys, passwords and connection strings that your app's Rayfin functions read on the server, without putting their values in your code."
---

Secrets are values such as API keys, passwords and connection strings that your app needs on the server but must never send to the browser. In the **Secrets** tab, you add them by name, and your app's Rayfin functions read them by name. Their values never go into your code or History.

Where a value is stored depends on the **Local development** experiment. With it off, the default, values are stored with your published app. With it on, each secret has a value on this computer, which your app uses while it runs here, and once the app is published, a value on the published app.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Only Rayfin functions can read secrets. Functions are available from Rayfin 1.36, but not in every Fabric region or tenant. See [Functions](https://rayfin.ai/docs/functions) in Rayfin's docs.

![The Secrets view of a published app with Local development on, listing OPENAI_API_KEY, SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL and STRIPE_SECRET_KEY with their local and published values, and the details of OPENAI_API_KEY, including the ctx.Secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY line a function uses to read it.](/screenshots/secrets.webp)

## Before you start

- With Local development off, publish your app first. Secrets are stored with your published app, so until it's published, the tab shows **Publish your app first**. With Local development on, you can add secrets before you publish.
- Use Rayfin 1.36 or newer. With an older version, the tab shows **Update Rayfin to use secrets**: select Rayfin in the status bar and choose **Update with Copilot**.
- To add or change secrets, use an app outside a team workspace. For a team app, the tab lists secrets but can't change them. See [Secrets in a team app](/docs/build/secrets#secrets-in-a-team-app).

## Open the Secrets tab

1. Open a project.
2. In the app bar, select **Code**.
3. In the code view's segmented control, select **Secrets**.

The tab lists each secret's name and description, and whether it has a value: under **Local value**, with Local development on, and under **Published value**, once the app is published. It never shows values: nobody can read a value back, not even you. With nothing selected, the side panel counts the secrets that have a value on this computer and on the published app.

## Values on this computer and on the published app

> [!WARNING]
> Local development is an experiment. Turn it on in **Settings → Experiments**. It may change or be removed in a future update.

With Local development on, each secret can have two values:

- **Local value**: what your app's functions read while the app runs on this computer. It's saved in the project's `.rayfin-local` folder, outside your code and History.
- **Published value**: what the published app's functions read. You can set it once the app is published.

The two are separate: setting one doesn't change the other. After you publish an app for the first time, give its secrets published values too.

A local value shows one of these:

| Local value | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **Set on this computer** | You set a value here. |
| **From your environment** | Your app uses the environment variable of the same name that Fabricator started with. To change it, change the variable and restart Fabricator. |
| **From local.settings.json** | Your app uses the value in `local.settings.json` in the functions folder. A value you set here is used instead. |
| **Not set** | Functions that read the secret fail when your app runs on this computer. Set a value to fix that. |

A published value shows **Set** or **Not set**, and **Couldn’t check** when Fabricator can't read your published app's values.

With Local development off, each secret has only a published value.

## Add a secret

1. Select **New secret**.
2. Type a **Name**. Fabricator writes names in capital letters with underscores, such as `OPENAI_API_KEY`. A name starts with a letter.
3. Paste the **Value**. To check what you pasted, select **Show value** (the eye button).
4. Optionally, fill in **What it’s for**. Never put the value here.
5. Select **Add secret**.

Fabricator adds the name and description to `rayfin/rayfin.yml`, updates the types that functions use, and saves that change to git history as "Add secret: NAME". Where the value goes depends on Local development:

- **On**: the value goes to this computer, as the secret's local value. Fabricator hands it straight to your app's local backend. For a published app, set its published value too.
- **Off**: Fabricator runs `rayfin secret set` and hands it the value directly, so the value is stored with your published app and isn't saved in your project or in Fabricator.

## Use a secret in a function

A function reads a secret by its name:

```ts
const apiKey = ctx.Secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY
```

Select a secret to see this line with a copy button. To have Copilot use the secret, select **Ask Copilot to use it**: Fabricator switches to **Build** and places a request about the secret in the chat composer, so you can add what the function should do before you send it. Copilot sees the secret's name, never its value.

```prompt title="Summarize expense notes with AI"
Add a Rayfin function that summarizes an expense's notes with the OpenAI API, using the OPENAI_API_KEY secret. Show the summary on the expense details page, with a loading state while it runs.
```

Read secrets only inside functions. Code that runs in the browser can't see secrets, and anything you put there is public. For how functions read secrets, see [Secrets in functions](https://rayfin.ai/docs/functions/secrets) in Rayfin's docs.

With Local development on, Copilot doesn't set secret values: when a function needs a new secret, it adds the name to `rayfin/rayfin.yml` and asks you to set the value here. It never asks for a value in chat.

## Set or replace a value

To set the value on this computer, with Local development on:

1. Select the secret.
2. Under **Local value**, select **Set**, or **Change** when it has a value.
3. Paste the value, then select **Set value** or **Change value**.

To set the value on the published app:

1. Select the secret.
2. Under **Published value**, select **Set value**, or **Replace value** when it has a value.
3. Paste the value, then select **Set value** or **Replace value**.

Functions get the new value from their next run. Because nobody can read a value back, keep the original in a safe place, such as your password manager or the service that issued it.

## Remove a local value

1. Select the secret.
2. Under **Local value**, select **Remove**, then confirm **Remove**.

Functions that read the secret fail when your app runs on this computer, until you set a value again. **Remove** appears for values you set here, not for values from your environment or `local.settings.json`.

## Delete a secret

1. Select the secret.
2. Under **Published value**, select **Delete**, then confirm **Delete**.

Fabricator removes the secret from your published app and from `rayfin/rayfin.yml`. Functions that read it stop working until you add it again. **Delete** appears when the published app has a value for the secret.

## Fix a secret that shows Not set

A secret's published value shows **Not set** when `rayfin/rayfin.yml` lists it but the published app has no value for it, for example after you publish the app to another Fabric workspace. Functions that read it fail in the published app.

1. Select the secret.
2. Under **Published value**, select **Set value**.
3. Paste its value, then select **Set value**.

With Local development on, a local value that shows **Not set** works the same way: under **Local value**, select **Set**.

A secret shows **Not in rayfin.yml** when it has a value but `rayfin/rayfin.yml` doesn't list it, so functions can't read it by name. To add it, set its published value again. If you don't need it, remove its value.

## Secrets in a team app

The pipeline of a [team workspace](/docs/team) deploys each app twice: the published app that everyone uses, and your preview. Each one keeps its own secrets, so your preview's functions read your preview's secrets, and the published app's functions read the published app's secrets.

For a team app, the **Secrets** tab lists the secrets of both under **Published app** and **Your preview**, but it can't add, replace or delete them yet. Until your preview deploys, **Your preview** shows "Not deployed yet. Your preview’s secrets show here once the pipeline deploys it." If a deploy fails, the tab still lists the secrets of the version that's live.

To add or change a team app's secret:

1. In the **Secrets** tab, select **Open in Fabric** next to **Published app** or **Your preview**. The app opens in the Fabric portal.
2. Add or change the secret there.
3. In Fabricator, select **Refresh** at the top of the tab.

**Ask Copilot to use it** works the same as for other apps. When the secret shows **Not in rayfin.yml**, the request also asks Copilot to add it to `rayfin/rayfin.yml`, so functions can read it by name.

## If the tab can't read your secrets

If the tab shows "Couldn’t read your published app’s secrets.", the message after it says why. When your Fabric sign-in has expired, it adds: "Your Fabric sign-in may have expired: open the account menu and select Refresh Fabric authentication, then try again." Do that, then select **Try again**.

With Local development on, if the tab says "Couldn’t check the values on this computer.", the message after it says why, and the local values show **Couldn’t check**. Fabricator reads them with the local backend that comes with it: if Windows blocked the local backend, see [Windows blocked rayfin-local](/docs/troubleshooting/preview#windows-blocked-rayfin-local).

If it still fails, see [Report a problem](/docs/troubleshooting/report-a-problem).
